title.en: Area of rectangles, triangles, parallelograms and trapezia

text.en: Two rectangles of rangoli: one 3 cm × 8 cm and one 4 cm × 7 cm. Which needs more powder if colouring evenly?

Area is the number of unit squares that cover a region, so a 3 cm by 8 cm rectangle has 24 square cm and a 4 cm by 7 cm rectangle has 28.
Perimeter is the length of the boundary, which is not a measure of area, because different shapes with the same perimeter can have very different areas.
A diagonal splits a rectangle into two congruent triangles, so a triangle's area is half of the rectangle: ½ × base × height.
Any triangle with base b and height h has area ½bh, because two copies make a parallelogram.
A parallelogram can be cut and moved to form a rectangle with the same base and height, so its area is base × height.
The height is the perpendicular distance between the base and the opposite side, not the slanted side.
A trapezium with parallel sides a and b and height h has area ½(a + b)h, the average of the parallel sides times height.
A rhombus or kite with diagonals d₁ and d₂ has area ½d₁d₂.
Area of a compound shape is found by splitting it into rectangles and triangles and adding.
Compressing a shape along one direction and stretching along another by the same factor keeps its area the same.

problem.en: A trapezium has parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 5 cm. Find its area.

prompt.en: Why is a triangle's area ½ × base × height?

requiredIdeas.en: Two equal triangles make a parallelogram.
A parallelogram has area base × height.

commonMisconceptions.en: Area of a triangle is base × height.

points.en: Rectangle: l × w; triangle: ½ b h; parallelogram: b × h.
Trapezium: ½(a + b)h; rhombus or kite: ½ d₁d₂.
Perimeter is not a measure of area.
